newsitem.title: USA: Mid Ocean sees more price pressure in '97.
newsitem.headline: Mid Ocean sees more price pressure in '97.

text.p: Mid Ocean Ltd said it believes there will be more pricing pressure in the rating environment in 1997 than in 1996.

Mid Ocean, in its 1996 annual report, also said it believes that certain ceding companies -- insurance companies that transfer risks to reinsurance companies -- may increase retentions while some may increase the upper limits of their reinsurance programs.
As a result, Bermuda-based Mid Ocean said, premiums in several segments of Mid Ocean's book of business may be down compared with fiscal 1996.
In addition, Mid Ocean said the favorable loss environment of the past four years may not continue.

However, premiums are expected to to be generated by the Brockbank Group, both as a result of an increase in the capacity of the two dedicated Lloyd's syndicates and the inclusion of four quarters of Brockbank operations in the 1997 accounts compared with only three in 1996.
Mid Ocean acquired a 51 percent stake in the Brockbank in December 1995.
Brockbank includes two Lloyd's dedicated syndicates and the associated managing agency.

During fiscal 1996, property catastrophe premium rates applicable to Mid Ocean's book of business, measured on an exposure adjusted basis, were down about six percent on major United States risks compared with fiscal 1995.
The United Kingdom, Japanese and Australian markets saw rates decline by about 11 percent, 16 percent and seven percent respectively, measured on the same basis.
Premiums ceded in fiscal 1996 were $40.6 million compared with $10.8 million in fiscal 1995, an increase of $29.8 million.
About $21.9 million of this increase was attributable to Brockbank, which as historically purchased a significant amount of reinsurance, Mid Ocean said.
Mid Ocean also said it purchased specific reinsurance protection covers at a cost of about $13.3 million.
These reinsurances were purchased to protect various aspects of Mid Ocean's book of business in response to a greater availablity of these covers at more attractive prices.
Mid Ocean said gross premiums written for the fiscal year ended October 31, 1996 were $566.3 million compared with $445.8 million in fiscal 1995, an increase of 27 percent.
This growth was attributable to the results of the Brockbank operation, which were included in the company's accounts for the first time.

Gross premiums written attributable to the two new dedicated Lloyd's syndicates managed by Brockbank amounted to $147.6 million while another syndicate, managed by Brockbank and reinsured by Mid Ocean, decreased by $21.5 million, resulting in a net increase of $126.1 million.
In the aggregate, gross premiums written on Mid Ocean's remaining book of business were flat.
However, Mid Ocean said the property catastrophe book decreased by $33.9 million.
The marine and energy book decreased by $6.4 million compared with fiscal 1995.
Those decreases were offset by increases in aviation and satellite and other lines, Mid Ocean said.
